title: Build shared RBAC v2 authorization library (policy eval, caching, standardized errors)
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
- RBAC v2 requires consistent permission checks across control plane services, API gateway, console backend, and selected admin/support tooling.
- Today checks are a mix of legacy RBAC v1 feature gates + ad-hoc org/project membership checks; this is causing inconsistent behavior and makes auditability difficult.

Goal
Deliver a shared authorization library (Go + TS) that:
1) Evaluates RBAC v2 policies using the chosen policy format/semantics (per ADR-014).
2) Provides a single, consistent call pattern for services to perform authz checks.
3) Implements low-latency caching suitable for hot paths.
4) Standardizes error handling and reason codes so console + API clients can explain denials and so audit logs can record consistent fields.

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Full integration across every service (tracked in integration issues).
- Changes to SSO/SAML identity mapping beyond what’s necessary to carry role IDs/claims into auth context.
- Data-plane inference authorization beyond existing tenant/project scoping.

Deliverables
A) Library API (Go)
- Core types: Resource, Action, Scope; Actor context (user/service/support session) and Target (org/project/etc).
- Single entrypoint: Authorize(ctx, actor, request) -> decision {allow/deny}, reason_code, policy_version, matched_rules (debug-only), evaluation_latency_ms.
- Standard error type that can map to HTTP 403 with machine-readable reason codes.

B) Library API (TypeScript)
- Same conceptual surface for console backend / node services.
- Error mapping helpers for consistent API responses.

C) Caching
- Cache policy bundle + role assignments at org scope.
- Cache key: org_id + policy_version (and optionally role_assignment_etag).
- Invalidation hooks: explicit invalidation when role assignments change; TTL fallback.
- Metrics: cache_hit, cache_miss, eval_latency_ms, invalidations_total, stale_read_suspected_total.

D) Standardized errors + reason codes
- Deny reasons must be stable and documented (for both debugging + UX):
  - AUTHZ_DENY_NO_PERMISSION
  - AUTHZ_DENY_SCOPE_MISMATCH
  - AUTHZ_DENY_UNKNOWN_ACTION
  - AUTHZ_DENY_POLICY_NOT_LOADED
  - AUTHZ_DENY_SUPPORT_SESSION_REQUIRED
  - AUTHZ_DENY_BREAK_GLASS_EXPIRED
  - AUTHZ_DENY_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT_STALE (diagnostic)
- Provide helper to attach structured log fields and to feed audit-log enrichment (actor, role_ids, policy_version, decision, reason_code).

Acceptance criteria
- A shared package exists and is imported by at least one production service (control plane) behind feature flag.
- Unit tests cover:
  - allow/deny correctness across multiple roles
  - deny-overrides behavior (per ADR)
  - unknown action behavior
  - scope matching logic (org-only vs project-scoped)
  - cache behavior + invalidation correctness
- Integration tests (in a downstream service) demonstrate consistent 403 responses and structured logging fields.
- Performance: p95 evaluation latency < 2ms on warm cache for typical requests (excluding network calls), and p95 < 10ms on cold cache.

Implementation notes / decisions
- Evaluation semantics per ADR-014 (deny overrides; explicit denies supported). The library should return the first matched explicit deny rule (for explainability) and otherwise an allow match (or default deny).
- Debug explainability: matched rule details must be gated (e.g., only in internal logs, never returned to customers by default).
- Service accounts: represent as ActorType=service with separately assigned roles (do not implicitly inherit org admin).
- Support/break-glass: include Actor attributes indicating elevated session ID + expiry; library should enforce "support session required" permissions by checking elevated-session claims.

Links
- ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-014-rbac-v2-policy-format.json
- Authz check standard: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/authz-check-standard.json
- Audit log enrichment spec: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/authz-decision-audit-logging.json

Rollout plan (owned by ENG-5389)
- Phase 1: library + middleware available; shadow evaluation (RBAC v1 enforced; RBAC v2 evaluated + logged).
- Phase 2: endpoint-by-endpoint enforcement under feature flag.
- Phase 3: default on for Hosted, then Dedicated, then Private (account for policy distribution/version skew).

Risks
- Cache invalidation correctness (role assignment updates must propagate quickly; stale allows are unacceptable).
- Divergence between Go and TS implementations; keep a shared conformance test corpus for policy fixtures.
- Partial adoption: ensure CI / conformance checks (later ticket) prevent new endpoints from bypassing checks.
comments: 2025-02-06 (Ethan Park): Marking this P0. ENG-5385/86/87 integrations are blocked on having the shared library surface + reason codes nailed down. Please coordinate with Jordan on evaluation semantics and with Kevin on audit fields.

2025-02-10 (Jordan Lee): Added initial policy evaluator implementation plan. Strongly recommend deny-overrides (explicit deny) for safety + audit needs. Need to ensure matched rule explainability doesn’t leak policy internals to customers.

2025-02-12 (Chloe Martin): Console backend needs stable reason codes so we can show actionable UI (e.g., "ask your admin for Billing Admin role"). Please avoid free-form strings; keep an enum list and document it.

2025-02-14 (Amara Diallo): For gateway integration: we need a fast path for common checks. If library always fetches role assignments over network, it will be too slow. Cache must be local + invalidation event-driven where possible.

2025-02-18 (Kevin Osei): Audit logging fields should include: policy_version, role_ids (list), decision=allow|deny, reason_code, and "authz_shadow" boolean when running in dual-eval. Please ensure library returns these in a structured decision object.

2025-02-21 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Implementing local in-process cache per org with explicit invalidation from role-assignment write paths (control plane). TTL fallback 60s. Adding metrics for cache hit rate + eval latency. TS implementation will share the same fixtures for conformance.

2025-02-27 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure break-glass / elevated sessions have an explicit expiry check in the library so we don’t rely on downstream callers to enforce it. Also need a reason code that distinguishes "needs elevated session" vs "elevated session expired" for incident debugging.

2025-03-04 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Go library merged behind feature flag; TS port ready for console backend follow-up. Added deny reason code mapping + standardized 403 response helper. Next: wire into more endpoints (ENG-5385) and enable shadow-deny dashboards (ENG-5389).

2025-03-11 (Connor O'Brien): Confirmed this is sufficient for starting dual-eval rollout in staging. Leaving follow-ups in ENG-5389 for any remaining perf tuning once we see real traffic distributions.
completion_notes: Shipped shared RBAC v2 authz types + evaluator hooks (Go) with policy caching and standardized 403 reason codes. Added metrics for evaluation latency + cache hit rate. Integrated into control plane middleware behind feature flag to unblock shadow evaluation + downstream endpoint integrations.
